title: Kubernetes lab: a three-node MicroK8s cluster
summary: A control plane and two workers on an isolated segment (172.20.6.0/24), MicroK8s 1.32 on Ubuntu 24.04 cloud images. The workers join the control plane by themselves at their first boot on the segment. The exercises read the cluster's anatomy, then run a Deployment of three nginx replicas spread over the nodes and reach it through a NodePort Service, from every node and from the host. Inspired by manzolo/multipass-microk8s-cluster-demo.

exercises.title: The cluster's anatomy
exercises.text: Three nodes, each with its address on the lab segment: the control plane runs the API server and is a node itself, the workers only run pods. kube-system holds the cluster's own pods: Calico (one per node, the pod network), CoreDNS, the metrics of nothing yet.

commands: kubectl get nodes -o wide          # three nodes Ready, INTERNAL-IP on 172.20.6.0/24
kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide    # calico-node on every node
microk8s status                    # acting as a node in a cluster: no control plane here

exercises.title: A Deployment and a NodePort Service
exercises.text: A Deployment keeps a number of identical pods running and the scheduler spreads them over the nodes. A Service gives them one address; a NodePort Service also opens the same port on every node, whichever node the pods run on. The control plane's 30080 is forwarded to the host's 8089.

commands: kubectl get pods -o wide           # NODE: the replicas spread over the nodes

for ip in $(kubectl get pods -l app=web -o jsonpath='{.items[*].status.podIP}'); do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$ip %{http_code}\n" http://$ip; done    # every pod from here, whatever its node: the pod network spans the cluster
for ip in 172.20.6.1 172.20.6.11 172.20.6.12; do curl -s http://$ip:30080 | grep -o '<title>.*</title>'; done    # every node answers
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8089 | grep -o '<title>.*</title>'    # the same page, from the host
kubectl delete pod $(kubectl get pods -l app=web -o name | head -n1 | cut -d/ -f2) && kubectl get pods -l app=web    # a new pod replaces it
kubectl scale deployment web --replicas=6 && kubectl get pods -o wide
kubectl delete service web && kubectl delete deployment web    # back to an empty default namespace
